# Sourdough Starter

## Ingredients

- 50 g active starter
- 250 g flour, split 125 g rye and 125 g wholemeal
- 250 g filtered water, room temperature

## Feeding Schedule

I keep mine on the counter in a 25 C kitchen and run a 12-hour cadence, once in the morning and once before bed. I discard half before feeding, then feed at a 1:5:5 ratio by weight (starter, flour, water). That means 50 g of kept starter gets 250 g of flour and 250 g of water. The flour is always a 50/50 rye and wholemeal mix, which keeps the culture vigorous and gives it a malty, slightly sour smell.

If I miss the timing the feeding ratio is forgiving, the culture just goes flat and a bit acidic. On cold mornings I warm the water to about 28 C. Weigh everything, scoops lie.

In a hot week the culture blows past its peak in eight hours, so I either shorten the cadence or park the jar in the coolest corner of the kitchen. In winter the same mix can crawl, and I give it a full 14 hours before touching it.

## Notes

A dark hooch layer on top is normal. It means the culture is hungry, not dead. Pour it off or stir it back in, then feed as usual.

In the fridge the same culture keeps up to two weeks without attention. It goes quiet and grey, which is fine.

To revive it from the fridge I pull it out, let it come to room temperature, and give two warm feeds about 12 hours apart. By the second feed it should double within six hours. If it does not, keep feeding every 12 hours until it does.

A healthy culture smells of yoghurt and green apple. If it smells of nail polish it is starving, so feed it more often for a few days and it recovers. I keep a small jar of dried flakes on the shelf as a backup, which has saved a batch twice. My oldest jar is four years old now and only gets stronger.
